qa.question: I attack my opponent using a Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards. If they block it with one of their Digimon, does this Digimon's effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes. Even if the Digimon is blocked, if you declared an attack against your opponent, the effect activates.

qa.question: I activate an effect that reads "Return 1 of your opponent's Digimon to their hand. Trash all of the digivolution cards of that Digimon" to return an opponent's Digimon to their hand. When your opponent's digivolution cards are trashed as a result, can you activate this card's inherited effect?
qa.answer:
No, you can’t.
Trash all of the digivolution cards of those Digimon"" is an explanation of what happens to the digivolution cards of the Digimon when it returns to their hand. It doesn't count as trashing digivolution for the purposes of this card's effect.

qa.question: I attack my opponent using a Digimon with this card in its digivolution cards. If they block it with one of their Digimon, does this card's effect activate?
qa.answer: No, if you declared an attack against your opponent, this card's effect doesn't activate, even if they use another Digimon to block it.

qa.question: I activate an effect that reads “<Draw 1> (Draw 1 card from your deck.) Then, trash 1 card in your hand.” Does this card’s inherited effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: I have 2 copies of this Digimon in my battle area. If I play a Tamer with [Tai Kamiya] in its name, can I activate the effects on both Digimon to gain a total of 2 memory?
qa.answer: Yes. The effects on both Digimon activate, so you gain 2 memory.

qa.question: I play a Tamer with [Tai Kamiya] in its name from my security using its security effect. If this Digimon’s effect causes the memory gauge to move to 1 or greater on my side, does it immediately become my turn?
qa.answer: No. The turn doesn’t switch over until the attack completely finishes resolving.

qa.question: I make a normal, non-<Blitz> attack with this Digimon. Can I use this card’s inherited effect to draw a card with <Draw 1>?
qa.answer: Yes. As long as a Digimon with <Blitz> is in this card’s digivolution cards, <Draw 1> will activate even if you make a normal, non-<Blitz> attack.

qa.question: This card’s effect reveals 2 copies of the same card with [Huckmon], [Jesmon], or [Sistermon] in their names from the top of my deck. Can I add both copies to my hand?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: If I have 2 Digimon with [Sistermon] in their names in play, can I use this card’s effect to delete 2 of my opponent’s Digimon with 5000 DP or less?
qa.answer: No. Even if you have multiple Digimon with [Sistermon] in their names in play, you can only use this Digimon’s effect to delete 1 of your opponent’s Digimon.

qa.question: Can this Digimon digivolve into a Digimon with “Black/Level 5” digivolution requirements?
qa.answer: Yes. During your turn, this Digimon is treated as both a red and black Digimon, so it can digivolve into a Digimon with black digivolution requirements.

qa.question: This card is in my breeding area. Can I digivolve it into a Digimon that requires a black Digimon?
qa.answer: No, you can't. [Your Turn] effects don't activate from breeding areas, so the card isn't treated as a black card. You can't digivolve it into a Digimon that requires a black Digimon.

qa.question: I use this Digimon’s [When Attacking] effect to play a Digimon card with [Sistermon] in its name. Does this Digimon’s [Your Turn] effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: When this Digimon digivolves, can I intentionally choose not to use a 7-cost Option card in my hand to delete 1 of my opponent’s Digimon with 4000 DP or less?
qa.answer: Yes, you can choose not to use an Option card. If you don’t use one, you can delete 1 of your opponent’s Digimon with 4000 DP or less.

qa.question: If I use this card’s [When Attacking] effect to delete 1 of my opponent’s Digimon with 13000 DP or less, can I use this card’s [Your Turn] effect to trash the top card of my opponent’s security stack?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: I have 2 copies of this Digimon in my battle area. If I play a Tamer with [Matt Ishida] in its name, can I activate the effects on both Digimon to gain a total of 2 memory?
qa.answer: Yes. The effects on both Digimon activate, so you gain 2 memory.

qa.question: Is a "while your opponent has no Digimon with XX" condition also met when my opponent has no Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, it's met.

qa.question: Does this card’s inherited effect activate when my opponent has no Digimon in play in their battle area?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: My opponent has this Digimon in play. What happens if an effect is activated that causes you to gain memory on activation and lose memory at end of turn? (i.e. [BT1-090 Gravity Crush], [BT1-021 MetalGreymon], [BT1-040 WereGarurumon], [BT1-058 Chirinmon], [BT1-075 Digitamamon], etc.)
qa.answer: You can't use Option/Digimon card effects to gain memory, but you can still lose memory if a card effect specifies as such. At the end of the turn, you’ll lose memory as specified by each effect.

qa.question: My opponent has this Digimon in play. Can I gain memory from the security effect of [ST2-13 Hammer Spark]?
qa.answer: No, this Digimon prevents you from gaining memory from security effects.

qa.question: Is a "while your opponent has no Digimon with XX" condition also met when my opponent has no Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, it's met.

qa.question: Does this card’s inherited effect activate when my opponent has no Digimon in play in their battle area?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: “Your Digimon can't be blocked by your opponent's Digimon this turn.” How does this effect work, exactly?
qa.answer: If you attack with a Digimon, your opponent's Digimon can’t change the target of attack by blocking.

qa.question: If this card's effect is activated on the opponent's turn, how long does the effect last?
qa.answer: When the effect of this card is activated on the opponent's turn, it lasts until the end of that turn.

qa.question: I have 2 Digimon with this card in their digivolution cards in my battle area, and a card is removed from my security stack. Do the inherited effects on both Digimon activate, activating <Draw 1> twice and drawing me 2 cards?
qa.answer: Yes. Both effects activate, so you can draw a total of 2 cards.

qa.question: When I play this card, does its [On Play] effect force me to trash cards from my security stack until there are 3 cards left?
qa.answer: No, this card’s [On Play] effect allows you to trash any number of cards, from zero cards, up to however many cards you need to trash for you to have 3 cards left in your security stack.

qa.question: How does this card’s [On Play] effect work if I have 3 or fewer cards in my security stack?
qa.answer: You can’t trash any security cards, so the effect does nothing.

qa.question: I have 5 cards in my security stack. Can I use this card’s [On Play] effect to only trash 1 security card and gain 1 memory?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: Does this card’s inherited effect activate when a security card is removed from my security stack by one of my own effects?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: Does this card’s inherited effect activate when a security card is removed from my security stack by one of my own effects?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: Can I activate this card’s effect when my security stack is empty?
qa.answer: No. You must trash a card from your security stack in order to have one of your opponent’s Digimon get -5000 DP.

qa.question: Does this card’s [When Digivolving] effect force me to trash the top card of my security stack?
qa.answer: No, this card’s [When Digivolving] effect reads “you may,” so you can choose whether or not to trash the top card of your security stack.

qa.question: Can I activate this card’s [When Digivolving] effect when my security stack is empty?
qa.answer: No. You must trash a card from your security stack in order to activate it.

qa.question: I use this card’s [When Digivolving] effect to trash a card from my security stack. If there are 3 or fewer cards left in my security stack, does this card’s [All Turns] effect trigger?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: I have 2 or more copies of this Digimon in play. My opponent attacks with a Digimon, removing a card from my security stack. Do all of the effects on copies of this Digimon activate simultaneously, activating <Recovery +1 (Deck)> for each one?
qa.answer:
Fundamentally, this is possible. However, the effects don’t activate simultaneously, but one at a time in order. Once <Recovery> results in you having 4 cards in your security stack, any remaining copies of the effect don't activate.
Any [BT6-044 Dynasmon] whose effects don’t activate can still be activated later in the turn.

qa.question: An opponent’s Digimon performs a security check, flipping over a card with a [Security] effect. Which activates first: This card’s [All Turns] effect, or the [Security] effect?
qa.answer:
The [Security] effect activates first.
After the [Security] effect and any effects triggered by its activation have finished activating, this card’s [All Turns] effect activates.

qa.question: I use this card’s effect to reveal 5 cards. If the cards revealed only include either a card with [Menoa Bellucci] in its name or a Digimon card with [Eosmon] in its name, can I still add a card to my hand?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. As long as either a card with [Menoa Bellucci] in its name or a Digimon card with [Eosmon] in its name are among the cards revealed, you can add it to your hand.

qa.question: Does a "may digivolve this card as if the Tamer is a Digimon" effect also treat the Tamer that will become a digivolution card as a Digimon when it digivolves?
qa.answer:
Yes, it also treats the Tamer as a Digimon when it digivolves. It treats it as a Digimon that digivolves, therefore "when a Digimon would digivolve" effects and "when a Digimon digivolves" effects will trigger.
In addition, if a "Digimon can't digivolve" effect activates, digivolution won't be possible using this effect that also treats the Tamer as a Digimon.

qa.question: Is a digivolution bonus draw performed even when a Tamer digivolves?
qa.answer:
Yes, you perform a digivolution bonus draw.
A digivolution bonus draw is performed for any kind of digivolution.

qa.question: If this card digivolves from a Tamer that was played this turn, can it attack in the same turn?
qa.answer:
No, it can't.
Even if a card digivolves from a card that was placed on the field in the same turn, it can't attack during that turn. It can only attack in the turns after it's played.

qa.question: Does a Tamer card placed under a Digimon become a digivolution card?
qa.answer:
Yes, it becomes a digivolution card.
If that Digimon would leave the field, the Tamer card will be trashed like a normal digivolution card.

qa.question: Does a Digimon gain the Security effect in the lower text on a Tamer card in digivolution cards?
qa.answer: No, it doesn't.

qa.question: Does a Digimon gain the Inherited effect in the lower text on a Tamer card in digivolution cards?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: Can I choose to not digivolve with this card's 1st effect?
qa.answer:
No, you can't.
For this card's 1st effect, you declare a digivolution, then upon revealing this card, you can also choose a Tamer as the card to digivolve, and that Tamer is also treated as a level 3 Digimon. As with the normal digivolution procedure, after revealing this card and declaring a digivolution, you can't choose to not digivolve.
In addition, you can't declare digivolution into this card in the first place unless there is a card on the field that you can digivolve.

qa.question: Does this card’s [Security] effect activate even if it loses the battle against the attacking Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, it activates at the end of the battle, regardless of outcome.

qa.question: This card is flipped over during a security check, but the attacking Digimon still has security checks remaining. Does this Digimon’s effect activate first, or do I have to wait until my opponent finishes the rest of their security checks?
qa.answer: This Digimon’s [Security] effect activates after the battle with the attacking Digimon ends, and before the next check is performed.

qa.question: If I use this card's effect to play a Digimon, is it treated as a Security Digimon even in my battle area?
qa.answer: No, it's treated as a normal Digimon once it comes into play.

qa.question: Can I play this Digimon with its [Security] effect even if it loses the battle against the attacking Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, regardless of the battle's outcome, you get to play this Digimon at the end of the battle.

qa.question: This card is flipped over during a security check, but the attacking Digimon still has security checks remaining. Is this card played off its [Security] effect first, or do I have to wait until my opponent finishes the rest of their security checks?
qa.answer: This Digimon is played after the battle with the attacking Digimon, and before the next check is performed.

qa.question: Can I digivolve this Digimon in the battle area into a card with the [Three Musketeers] trait in the hand when an effect to digivolve one of my Digimon is activated?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: When does this card's [All Turns] effect trigger, exactly?
qa.answer:
It will trigger when a Digimon is played by an effect such as the effect on BT5-092 [Nokia Shiramine] or when a Digimon digivolves by an effect such as the effect on P-103 [Offense Training].
It won't trigger for effects that aren't digivolution effects, such as BT4-011 [Agunimon]'s effect that treats a Tamer as a level 3 red Digimon or BT6-060 [Deputymon]'s effect that allows digivolution requirements to be ignored.

You can’t ignore digivolution requirements because it isn't treated as a card in the hand.

If you don’t use it, you delete 1 of your opponent’s Digimon with a play cost of 4 or less.

qa.question: If I have 4 or fewer cards in my deck, does this Digimon’s [When Digivolving] effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes, it does. Reveal as many cards from your deck as you can, then perform the rest of the effect as normal.

qa.question: What does “Delete all of your opponent's Digimon with the lowest play cost” mean, exactly?
qa.answer: The effect deletes your opponent’s Digimon with the lowest play cost. If multiple Digimon are tied for lowest, all of them are deleted.

qa.question: My opponent only has 1 unsuspended Digimon in play, and I attack with this Digimon. When my opponent blocks and suspends their unsuspended Digimon, does my attacking Digimon immediately lose <Security Attack +1> from this card’s effect?

qa.answer:
No, the effect reads “you may,” so you can choose whether or not to trash the card.
If you don't trash a card, you don’t get to return a Digimon card with [Seven Great Demon Lords] or [Three Musketeers] in its type from your trash to your hand.

qa.question: Can I activate this card’s effect when my hand is empty?
qa.answer: No. You must trash a card in your hand in order to activate it.

qa.question: Can I use this card’s [On Play] effect to place a [Ginkakumon Promote] from my trash in this card’s digivolution cards?
qa.answer: No. This card’s [On Play] effect can only be used to place cards whose names match either [Kinkakumon] or [Ginkakumon] exactly, therefore you can't place [Ginkakumon Promote] in digivolution cards.

qa.question: If I have both [Kinkakumon] and [Ginkakumon] in my trash, does this card’s [On Play] effect force me to place both cards in this card’s digivolution cards?
qa.answer: No, "You may place..." means that you can choose if you want to place them as digivolution cards or not. However, if you choose to place, you must place as many digivolution cards as possible. So, if you have both [Kinkakumon] and [Ginkakumon], you can't choose to place only one of them.

qa.question: This card is in my breeding area. Can I digivolve it into a Digimon that requires a black Digimon?
qa.answer: No, you can't. Effects don't activate from breeding areas, so the card isn't treated as a black card. You can't digivolve it into a Digimon that requires a black Digimon.

qa.question: Can I activate this card’s effect when my hand is empty?
qa.answer: No. You must trash a card in your hand in order to activate it.

qa.question: I have 9 cards in my trash when this Digimon is deleted. If this results in my having 10 cards in my trash, does this card’s [On Deletion] effect activate?
qa.answer: Yes. The [On Deletion] effect activates after the card moves to your trash, meeting the requirement for you to have 10 cards in your trash.

qa.question: This card's [When Digivolving] effect placed a [BT10-016 Jesmon (X Antibody)] as a digivolution card, then that card's [When Digivolving] effect played a [BT6-082 Sistermon Blanc], then I activated <Blitz> in this card's [When Digivolving] effect to attack. When does [BT6-082 Sistermon Blanc]'s [On Play] effect activate?
qa.answer:
Since both the [BT6-082 Sistermon Blanc] having been played and this Digimon attacking with <Blitz> happened during this Digimon's [When Digivolving] effect, the Digimon being played and the attack are treated as having happened at the same time for the purpose of triggering effects.
The turn player can choose the order in which to activate the [On Play] effect and any potential [When Attacking] and such effects.

qa.question: This card's [When Digivolving] effect placed a [BT10-016 Jesmon (X Antibody)] as a digivolution card, then that card's [When Digivolving] effect played a [BT6-082 Sistermon Blanc], then I activated <Blitz> in this card's [When Digivolving] effect to attack, and when the [When Attacking] effect deleted one of my opponent's Digimon, my [BT6-082 Sistermon Blanc] was deleted by the [On Deletion] effect of the opponent's Digimon. [BT6-082 Sistermon Blanc]'s [On Play] effect hasn't activated yet, so does it activate?
qa.answer:
No, it doesn't activate.
The [On Play] effect from [BT6-082 Sistermon Blanc] was triggered, but it cannot activate because the [Sistermon Blanc] is deleted before it is able to activate.

qa.question: If I don’t play a Tamer using this card’s [On Play] effect, does that prevent my opponent from playing a Tamer card, as well?
qa.answer: No. Even if you choose not to play a Tamer, your opponent can still use this card’s effect to play a Tamer of their own.

qa.question: My BT6-083 [Eosmon] was played, then this card's [All Turns] effect and another effect triggered simultaneously. If another effect activates and the DP of my played BT6-083 [Eosmon] changes from 4000 to 5000, then I activate this card's [All Turns] effect, what is the DP of Digimon I can delete?
qa.answer:
5000 DP or less.
If the same reference to a "played" trigger condition being performed isn't being made for an effect when it has a "when X is played" trigger condition, the state when the effect is processed will be referenced.
In this case, processing was performed when your BT6-083 [Eosmon] had 5000 DP, therefore you can delete a Digimon with 5000 DP or less.

qa.question: What does this card's (Rule) mean, exactly? (*This card's "Also treated as Name: [Sistermon Noir] and Trait: [Virus]" has been changed to "(Rule) Also treated as Name: [Sistermon Noir] and Trait: [Virus]")
qa.answer: This is a special rule for this card that always treats it as if it also has the name [Sistermon Noir] and the [Virus] trait.

qa.question: I have BT10-085 [Sistermon Ciel]. Can I use this card's [When Digivolving] [When Attacking] effect to play a BT6-084 [Sistermon Ciel] or ST12-13 [Sistermon Ciel] that's also treated as [Sistermon Noir]?
qa.answer:
No, it can't be played.
"With the same names" also refers to a card with even just 1 of the same name as any of your Digimon.
This effect can't play cards with the same name as [Sistermon Ciel].

qa.question: What does this card's (Rule) mean, exactly? (*This card's "You can include up to 50 copies of cards with this card's card number in your deck" has been changed to "(Rule) You can include up to 50 copies of cards with this card's card number in your deck")
qa.answer: This is a specific rule that allows you to include up to 50 copies of cards with this card's card number in your deck.

qa.question: I use this card while I have 1 [ST1-12 Tai Kamiya] in play, and play a [BT6-085 Eosmon] from my hand. [ST1-12 Tai Kamiya]’s effect gives [BT6-085 Eosmon] +1000 DP, bringing it up to a total of 7000 DP. Can I delete 1 of my opponent’s Digimon with 7000 DP or less?
qa.answer: Yes. If a DP-boosting effect activates when you play a Digimon, the Digimon’s modified DP value is referenced by this card’s effect. You can delete 1 of your opponent’s Digimon with DP less than or equal to [Eosmon]’s boosted DP.

qa.question: I only have 1 or fewer cards left in my security stack. Can I activate this card’s [Main] effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
If you do, trash as many cards from your security stack as you can.

qa.question: Can I use this card’s [Main] effect on cards with [Agumon] in their name? (For example, [Agumon Expert], [ToyAgumon], etc.)
qa.answer: No, this card’s [Main] effect only affects cards whose names are [Agumon].

qa.question: I activated this card’s [Main] effect to digivolve into [Agumon - Bond of Bravery]. I had 1 or more cards in my security stack at the time of activation, but another effect causes my security stack to become empty later that same turn. Do I get to keep [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] in play at the end of the turn?
qa.answer: No. If you had 1 or more cards in your security stack at the time the effect finished activating, [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] will be deleted at the end of the turn, regardless of how many cards are in your security stack at that time.

qa.question: I have 2 copies of this card in play. I use the first copy’s [Main] effect to digivolve a Digimon into an [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] while there are 1 or more cards in my security stack. I use the second copy’s [Main] effect to digivolve a different Digimon into [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] while my security stack is empty. What happens to each [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] at the end of the turn?
qa.answer:
The first copy’s effect was used to digivolve into [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] while your security stack had 1 or more cards in it, so [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] will be deleted at the end of the turn.
The second copy’s effect was used to digivolve into [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] while your security stack was empty, so [Agumon - Bond of Bravery] stays in play at the end of the turn.

qa.question: Do I delete the Digimon that digivolved by this card's effect at the end of the same turn it digivolved?
qa.answer: Yes, it's deleted upon the deletion timing.

qa.question: What is the processing order for an effect that triggers at the end of the turn and the deletion of a Digimon that digivolved by this card's [Main] effect?
qa.answer: The pending processing for the effect that triggers at the end of the turn and the deletion at the end of the turn are considered to be processing that triggers simultaneously. Therefore, the turn player can choose the processing order.

qa.question: I only have 1 or fewer cards left in my security stack. Can I activate this card’s [Main] effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, you can.
If you do, trash as many cards from your security stack as you can.

qa.question: I activated this card’s [Main] effect to digivolve into [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship]. I had 1 or more cards in my security stack at the time of activation, but another effect causes my security stack to become empty later that same turn. Do I get to keep [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] in play at the end of the turn?
qa.answer: No. If you had 1 or more cards in your security stack at the time the effect finished activating, [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] will be deleted at the end of the turn, regardless of how many cards are in your security stack at that time.

qa.question: "I have 2 copies of this card in play. I use the first copy’s [Main] effect to digivolve a Digimon into a [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] while there are 1 or more cards in my security stack. I use the second copy’s [Main] effect to digivolve a different Digimon into [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] while my security stack is empty. What happens to each [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] at the end of the turn?"
qa.answer:
The first copy’s effect was used to digivolve into [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] while your security stack had 1 or more cards in it, so [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] will be deleted at the end of the turn.
The second copy’s effect was used to digivolve into [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] while your security stack was empty, so [Gabumon - Bond of Friendship] stays in play at the end of the turn.

qa.question: Do I delete the Digimon that digivolved by this card's effect at the end of the same turn it digivolved?
qa.answer: Yes, it's deleted upon the deletion timing.

qa.question: What is the processing order for an effect that triggers at the end of the turn and the deletion of a Digimon that digivolved by this card's [Main] effect?
qa.answer: The pending processing for the effect that triggers at the end of the turn and the deletion at the end of the turn are considered to be processing that triggers simultaneously. Therefore, the turn player can choose the processing order.

qa.question: The number of cards in my security stack is equal to the number of cards in my opponent’s security stack. Does this card’s [Start of Your Turn] effect activate?
qa.answer: No, this card’s [Start of Your Turn] effect only activates “if you have fewer security cards than your opponent,” so if you and your opponent both have the same number of security cards, it won’t activate.

qa.question: Does this card’s [Start of Your Turn] effect allow me to gain 2 memory if my opponent has no Digimon in play in their battle area?
qa.answer: Yes, it does.

qa.question: "If you have a Digimon with [Three Musketeers] in its type in play, you may use this Option card without meeting its color requirements.” How does this effect work, exactly?
qa.answer: If you have a Digimon with [Three Musketeers] in its type in play in your battle area, you can use this Option card even if you don’t have a red Digimon or Tamer in play.

qa.question: What does “all of your opponent's Digimon with the lowest DP” mean, exactly?
qa.answer: The effect deletes your opponent’s Digimon with the lowest DP. If multiple Digimon are tied for lowest, all of them are deleted.

qa.question: I use this card’s effect to prevent one of my opponent’s Digimon with no digivolution cards from attacking or blocking. If that Digimon later gains a digivolution card, can it attack and block?
qa.answer: No. This card’s effect is already activated, so the affected Digimon can’t attack or block until the effect ends.

qa.question: I use this card’s effect to trash 2 digivolution cards from the bottom of 1 of my opponent’s Digimon. For the part of this card’s effect that reads “1 of your opponent's Digimon with no digivolution cards can't attack or block until the end of your opponent's next turn,” can I choose a different Digimon with no digivolution cards other than the one I trashed digivolution cards from using the first part of this card’s effect?
qa.answer: Yes, you can.

qa.question: Can I use this card if I have 0 cards left in my security stack?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. The second half of the effect still occurs even if you don’t have a security card to trash.

qa.question: When using this card’s effect to place a card on top of my security stack, do I need to show it to my opponent?
qa.answer: Yes. You're revealing cards from your deck, which means they’re public information until you choose one to place face down on top of your security stack. You must show the card you place in your security stack to your opponent first.

qa.question: Can I use this card if I have 1 or fewer cards left in my deck?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. Reveal as many cards from your deck as you can, then perform the rest of the effect as normal.

qa.question: I use this card’s effect to give “[On Deletion] Lose 2 memory.” to an opponent’s Digimon. What happens when that Digimon is deleted?
qa.answer:
Your opponent loses 2 memory, which means you gain 2 memory.
If you use this card to give “[On Deletion] Lose 2 memory” to an opponent’s Digimon, you gain 2 memory when that Digimon is deleted.

qa.question: I used an effect like [BT6-103 Blasted Disaster] that suspends multiple DIgimon to simultaneously suspend 2 of my opponent's Digimon with 6000 DP or less. In such cases, can I use this card's [All Turns] effect to delete those 2 Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes you can, as long as they are simultaneously suspended.

qa.question: "If you have a Digimon with [Three Musketeers] in its type in play, you may use this Option card without meeting its color requirements.” How does this effect work, exactly?
qa.answer: If you have a Digimon with [Three Musketeers] in its type in play in your battle area, you can use this Option card even if you don’t have a black Digimon or Tamer in play.

qa.question: Does this card’s effect also delete all of my Digimon with play costs of 7 or less?
qa.answer: Yes. Both your and your opponent delete all Digimon with play costs of 7 or less.

qa.question: What does “all of your opponent's Digimon with the highest play cost” mean, exactly?
qa.answer: The effect deletes your opponent’s Digimon with the highest play cost. If multiple Digimon are tied for highest, all of them are deleted.

qa.question: Can I use this card if I don't have any Digimon cards in my trash?
qa.answer: Yes, you can. The second half of the effect still occurs even if you don’t have a Digimon card to return from your trash.

qa.question: "If you have a Digimon with [Three Musketeers] in its type in play, you may use this Option card without meeting its color requirements.” How does this effect work, exactly?
qa.answer: If you have a Digimon with [Three Musketeers] in its type in play in your battle area, you can use this Option card even if you don’t have a purple Digimon or Tamer in play.

qa.question: I use this card while I have 1 [ST1-12 Tai Kamiya] in play, and play a [BT6-085 Eosmon] from my hand. [ST1-12 Tai Kamiya]’s effect gives [BT6-085 Eosmon] +1000 DP, bringing it up to a total of 7000 DP. Can I delete 1 of my opponent’s Digimon with 7000 DP or less?
qa.answer: Yes. If a DP-boosting effect activates when you play a Digimon, the Digimon’s modified DP value is referenced by this card’s effect. You can delete 1 of your opponent’s Digimon with DP less than or equal to [Eosmon]’s boosted DP.

qa.question: Does this card’s [Security] effect activate even if it loses the battle against the attacking Digimon?
qa.answer: Yes, it activates at the end of the battle, regardless of outcome.

qa.question: If I use this card’s [Security] effect to prevent my opponent’s currently attacking Digimon from attacking players, does the attack end immediately, or does my opponent get to perform their remaining security checks?
qa.answer: Even after using this card’s [Security] effect to prevent your opponent’s Digimon from attacking players, it only prevents them from declaring further attacks. The current attack proceeds normally.

qa.question: My opponent uses this card’s [Security] effect to prevent one of my Digimon with <Piercing> from attacking players. If that Digimon attacks and deletes an opponent's Digimon and survives, do I still get to perform security checks with <Piercing>?
qa.answer: Yes, you do.

qa.question: I have 11 or fewer Digimon in play, and my opponent activates this card’s [Security] effect, preventing all of my Digimon from attacking players for the turn. If I later play a Digimon with <Rush> during that same turn, can that Digimon attack players?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can.
This card’s [Security Effect] only affects Digimon that are in play at the time it’s activated.

qa.question: If this Digimon attacks and is deleted in battle, does its [End of Attack] effect activate at the end of the attack?
qa.answer: No, it doesn’t.

qa.question: When using this card’s [On Play] effect to use an Option card, can I use any 7-cost Option card, regardless of its color requirements?
qa.answer: No, you can’t ignore its color requirements.

qa.question: Can I use option cards that can change their cost to 7 on certain conditions such as [BT7-100 Qualialise Blast] or [BT11-108 DG Dimension] with this card’s [On Play] effect?
qa.answer:
No, you can’t. Since those options are cards that have effects that “reduce the cost by…” or “its memory cost is equal to…” when they would be used, their cost has not actually changed when activating this card’s [On Play] effect, so they can’t be used with this card’s effect.
However, since [BT2-099 Glorious Burst] always has the effect of reducing its use cost when used from the hand, if you have 2 yellow Tamers, it can be used with this card’s effect as its use cost will be 7.

comprehensive-0223.title: <Blocker>
comprehensive-0223.text:
16-5. <Blocker>
16-5-1. <Blocker> is a keyword effect that applies a rule that allows a Digimon with that effect to block. (For details, refer to 12 "Blocking")
16-5-2. <Blocker> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-5-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Blocker>, the number of blocks that can be performed during the block timing is only 1.

comprehensive-0224.title: <Recovery>
comprehensive-0224.text:
16-6. <Recovery>
16-6-1. <Recovery> is a keyword effect where the specified number of cards from the specified area are placed face down on top of the security stack. This is shown on cards using text such as <Recovery +1>.
16-6-2. <Recovery> effects execute processing.

comprehensive-0225.title: <Piercing>
comprehensive-0225.text:
16-7. <Piercing>
16-7-1. <Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
16-7-2. <Piercing> is a trigger-type effect that triggers and activates when a Digimon with this effect battles an opponent's Digimon and the opponent's Digimon is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
16-7-3. The security check from using <Piercing> is mandatory.
16-7-4. <Piercing> is pending processing that is processed immediately before the transition to the end of attack timing. Therefore, it will trigger simultaneously with effects triggered by the battle, but it is processed before the end of the attack. (Example: If a Digimon with <Piercing> attacks and deletes a Digimon with an [On Deletion] effect in the battle, first the [On Deletion] effect is resolved, then <Piercing> is processed.)
16-7-5. Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack, even if <Piercing> activates multiple times. However, if the number of cards that can be checked by the attacking Digimon is modified, that number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
16-7-6. If there are no Digimon to perform a security check at the point when <Piercing> is processed, a security check won't be possible.

comprehensive-0226.title: <Draw>
comprehensive-0226.text:
16-8. <Draw>
16-8-1. <Draw> is a keyword effect where a player draws the cards from their deck according to the number specified in the effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Draw 1>.
16-8-2. <Draw> effects execute processing.
16-8-3. A draw from <Draw> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0227.title: <Jamming>
comprehensive-0227.text:
16-9. <Jamming>
16-9-1. <Jamming> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect isn't deleted as a result of a battle with an opponent's Security Digimon.
16-9-2. <Jamming> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0229.title: <Reboot>
comprehensive-0229.text:
16-11. <Reboot>
16-11-1. <Reboot> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect is unsuspended during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-2. <Reboot> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-11-3. Even if 1 Digimon has multiple instances of <Reboot>, it is only unsuspended once during the opponent's unsuspend phase.
16-11-4. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is mandatory.
16-11-5. The unsuspending from <Reboot> is performed at the same time as the unsuspending of the turn player's Digimon. The unsuspends aren't performed in any particular order.

comprehensive-0230.title: <De-Digivolve>
comprehensive-0230.text:
16-12. <De-Digivolve>
16-12-1. <De-Digivolve> is a keyword effect where the player declares a number from 1 up to the number specified in the effect, then the declared number of cards are trashed from the chosen stack(s) of cards starting with the top card. This is shown on cards using text such as <De- Digivolve 1>.
16-12-2. <De-Digivolve> effects execute processing.
16-12-3. The trashing from <De-Digivolve> is mandatory. Once activated, a player can't choose to trash 0 cards.
16-12-4. <De-Digivolve> can't trash cards from level 3 cards or lower.
16-12-5. If multiple cards are trashed using 1 instance of <De- Digivolve>, all of the cards are considered to be trashed at the same time, but the procedure for trashing them is 1 card from the stack at a time.
16-12-6. When using <De-Digivolve> to trash multiple cards, even if the category of the top card changes while the trashing is still being performed, the trashing will continue until the declared number is trashed.
16-12-7. When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the processing is performed separately for each instance.
16-12-8. When separate instances of <De-Digivolve> are executed multiple times in a single effect, the state of the chosen card is confirmed after each single process for <De-Digivolve> ends. If an effect will be activated as a result of the confirmed state, it is then activated. (Example: When 3 instances of <De-Digivolve 1> are executed in a single effect, if the chosen card becomes an "unaffected by effects" card as a result of the 1st instance of <De-Digivolve 1>, that card is unaffected by the following instances of <De-Digivolve 1>.

comprehensive-0231.title: <Retaliation>
comprehensive-0231.text:
16-13. <Retaliation>
16-13-1. <Retaliation> is a keyword effect where a battled opponent's Digimon is deleted when a Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle.
16-13-2. <Retaliation> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when just the Digimon with this effect is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-13-3. The processing from <Retaliation> is mandatory.

comprehensive-0232.title: <Digi-Burst>
comprehensive-0232.text:
16-14. <Digi-Burst>
16-14-1. <Digi-Burst> is a keyword effect where another effect specified by this effect will activate by trashing the specified number of digivolution cards from the Digimon with this effect. This is shown on cards using text such as <Digi-Burst 1>.
16-14-2. The processing from <Digi-Burst> is optional. For details, refer to 15-6 "Processing Conditions")

comprehensive-0233.title: <Rush>
comprehensive-0233.text:
16-15. <Rush>
16-15-1. <Rush> is a keyword effect where the Digimon with this effect can also attack in the same turn it was played.
16-15-2. <Rush> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")

comprehensive-0234.title: <Blitz>
comprehensive-0234.text:
16-16. <Blitz>
16-16-1. <Blitz> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect can attack if your opponent has 1 or more memory.
16-16-2. <Blitz> effects execute processing.
16-16-3. <Blitz> has a processing condition that requires the memory to be at 1 or more on your opponent's side. "This Digimon may attack" is optional processing.
16-16-4. After using <Blitz> to make an attack declaration, the attack will proceed even if the memory moves to 0 or more.38
16-16-5. An attack can't be made using <Blitz> if the memory is at 0 or more upon activating <Blitz>.

comprehensive-0235.title: <Delay>
comprehensive-0235.text:
16-17. <Delay>
16-17-1. <Delay> is a keyword effect. While a card with this effect is in the battle area, by trashing that card, the effect specified in <Delay> will activate.
16-17-2. The processing from <Delay> is optional. (For details, refer to 15-7 "Optional Processing Conditions")
16-17-3. <Delay> can't be activated the same turn the card with the effect is placed in the battle area.

comprehensive-0236.title: <Decoy>
comprehensive-0236.text:
16-18. <Decoy>
16-18-1. <Decoy> is a keyword effect. When another of your specified Digimon would be deleted by an opponent's effect, by deleting the Digimon with this effect, <Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted. This is shown on cards using text such as <Decoy (Black)>.
16-18-2. <Decoy> is an immediate-type effect that triggers when another of your Digimon specified by this effect would be deleted by an opponent's effect (For details, refer to 15-8-5 "Immediate-Type Effects")
16-18-3. "By deleting this Digimon" in <Decoy> is an optional processing condition. If the content of that condition is executed, the processing for "<Decoy> prevents the Digimon specified by this effect from being deleted" will be mandatory.
